answer: No doc states how `ctx_upgrade mode:uninstall` gets user confirmation for data removal when it runs headless over MCP. ADR-0010 Q16 only says user data is kept unless the user confirms, but there is no confirm channel defined: no elicitation/sampling call, no CLI prompt, no separate confirmation argument. On agents with no interactive UI in front of the MCP call (Kiro, ZCode, Pi), there is no way for the tool to ask and no way for the model to pass real consent back. As written, calling mode:uninstall on these agents will either always skip data removal (safe but silently wrong, since the agent cannot explain why data stayed) or an agent could pass a hardcoded confirm:true with no real user behind it (unsafe, silent data loss). This is an owner decision: the safest fix is to require a single explicit tool argument, for example confirmSUniqueToken or a typed confirmation string the user must have stated in-session, and when it is absent on any agent, interactive or not, treat mode:uninstall as data-preserving by default and return a message telling the agent to re-run with the confirmation argument once the user has actually said yes.
evidence: docs/v2/adr/0010-doctor-and-upgrade.md:69 states only 'user data is kept unless the user confirms' with no mechanism named. grep across docs/v2/adr/0012-keyless-live-harness.md and docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md for elicit/sampling/UI/interactive near 'confirm' returned nothing. docs/v2/review/OWNER-QUESTIONS-r3.md:77 Q16 only asks whether uninstall exists and stops the server/removes cache -- it does not ask about the confirmation mechanism, so this question was never raised in r3 and DECISIONS-r3.md has no ruling on it.

finding.claim: ADR-0010 Q16 says data removal in ctx_upgrade mode:uninstall requires user confirmation, but defines no confirmation mechanism for headless MCP calls on agents with no interactive UI (Kiro, ZCode, Pi).
finding.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0010-doctor-and-upgrade.md:69: 'user data is kept unless the user confirms' -- no elicitation, sampling, CLI prompt, or confirmation argument is specified anywhere in TECH-SPEC.md or the ADRs.
finding.fix: Add to ADR-0010: mode:uninstall requires an explicit tool argument carrying real user consent (e.g. a confirmation string the user must have typed in this session). If the argument is missing, always keep user data and return a message asking the agent to get the user's explicit yes first, regardless of whether the host agent has an interactive UI.
